div.ab: Ara ðinum fæder ⁊ þinre medder, ða þe Dryhten sealde, þæt ðu sie þy leng libbende on eorþan.
Ara ðinum fæder ⁊ þinre meder, ða þe Drihten sealde, þæt ðu sie ðy leng libbende on eorþan.
Ara þinum fæder ⁊ þinre meder, þa þe Drihten sealde, þæt ðu sy þe leng libbende on eorðan.
Honora patrem tuum et matrem tuam, ut sis longeuus super terram quam dominus Deus tuus dabit tibi.
Ara ðinum fæder ⁊ þinre medder, ða þe Dryhten sealde, þæt ðu sie þy leng libbende on eorþan.
Ehre deinen Vater und deine Mutter, die dir der Herr gab, auf dass du desto länger lebest auf Erden.
Honour your father and your mother, whom the Lord gave you, so that you may live the longer on earth.
Honor your father and mother, they whom the Lord gave you, so that you may live long on the earth.

note.seg: þæt þu sie þy l. libbend on e., þa þe Drihtene þe gesealde So, nach Vulgata
þæt þu sie þy l. libbend on e., þa þe Drihtene þe gesealde So, following the Vulgate
sy ðy l. libbend on eorþum Ld
sy ðy l. libbend on eorþum Ld

S. El 14; Gl Eltern. Dass etwa Ælfred nur irrig quos statt quam verstand, glaube ich nicht. Da jedoch der Relativsatz in Ælfrics Dekalog fehlt, so mag er vielleicht auch in Ælfreds Original am Rande nachgetragen worden und beim Übersetzen an falsche Textstelle geraten sein. Hs. So bleibt der Vulgata treu

See El 14; Gl Eltern. I do not believe that Ælfred, say, merely misunderstood quam as quos. Since, however, the relative clause is absent from Ælfric’s Decalogue, it may perhaps also have been added in the margin in Ælfred’s original and have got into the wrong place in translation. MS So remains faithful to the Vulgate
